**Read this first.** This is the first release whose centre is new content rather than
restoration, because Montserrat is the first place the shipped game plainly ran out: five maps,
one conversation, sixty identical fights. Parts of it have been played once -- the Grove, the
wounded assassin, Sahar's approach, the journal's return -- and repaired from what that found;
the boss fight's phases, the abbey's hover trail and most of the build levers are built and
unplayed. If you would rather wait for a build somebody has walked end to end, wait.

## Montserrat

**The road in.** The packs are no longer eight recolours of one snake: human assassins walk with
them, and a priestess in the larger packs who has to die first. A sentry calls two packs down on
you if you wound him and live -- kill him in one blow and nobody comes. An ambush waits in the
hall, a poisoned tripwire before the inner door, a trapped chest in the sanctum's first room; a
thief finds and steps over all of it.

**The dead speak.** Sir Tomas de Vilanova led the Templars who never came back; he lies at the
gate with his journal, three entries, and whoever sent you to Montserrat will take it from you
and see it reaches Lord Javier. Among the dead in the hall, one of the killers is still
breathing: ask him who sent them (Speech), where they went, why; finish him or leave him; a
Demokin gets the road without asking, an Aswaran gets a word about the Crescent. Brother Michel
will hear what you learned.

**Sahar.** The rearguard's captain waits at the reliquary with two of the creatures and the
priestess behind her, and speaks before she fights. She calls the hall's survivors at half her
strength and is healed at a quarter. Outwit her -- claim to be Machiavelli's courier -- and her
crew stands down and she fights alone. Only when everything near Montgomerie is dead does he
speak, and now the voiced line about how long ago it happened plays.

**The abbey.** The sanctum has an altar, a cross, pews and a burned banner; ten things to click
between the gate and the reliquary tell you what happened here -- the camp the knights slept in
once, the barricade broken from the inside, the candles still burning, the druid gate older than
the abbey, the reliquary open and empty. Perception reads more; a Wielder, a Sylvant, an
Inquisitor and an Educated character each read something the others do not. And nobody explains
why there is not one monk among the dead.

## Also since 0.9.4

- Quinn's reserve is gone: the potions you earn appear in his ordinary shop, and his errands
  and goodbye sit where a menu expects them. (Old saves keep the reserve, on the greeting.)
- The Desoto brothers: Juan thanks you, walks to Fernand, and gets told off for fishing off the
  north island alone. He is a dying man now, not a corpse -- the spirit skills cannot take him
  -- and he warns you at twenty seconds if you are slow.
- The Vodyanoi Anatomist perk does what it says, with fists, blades, bows or spells alike.
- The Knights of Saladin's cathedral summit plays and ends; Enrique's red-ore argument opens;
  the peaceful road through the sewers reaches both the troll hide and the wererat cure.
- The 0.9.1 Mongol Camp crash, fixed in 0.9.4, and a build check so it cannot ship again.

## Installing

Download, unzip, run `Mod Manager.bat`. It installs over any earlier release.

**Montserrat needs a character who has never entered it.** Quinn's merged shop needs one who has
not entered his shop; the Port District pieces one who has not entered the district; the
cathedral one who has not entered it. Dialogue-only pieces -- the journal's return, the perk,
Enrique, the chief -- work on any save.
